case_description: Someone stole my mobile phone from my pocket in a crowded bus.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 34 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek to institute a complaint against the perpetrator(s) for the alleged commission of the offence of 'dishonestly misappropriating property' under Article 265 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 265(1)(b) read with Article 265(2).

Under Article 23 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, I request the registering of a First Information Report (FIR) and an investigation be initiated under Article 26(1) of the same Act.

Pursuant to Article 13 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, I seek to adduce evidence of the occurrence, including the fact that the mobile phone was in my possession prior to its alleged theft and that it was stolen during the commotion in the crowded bus.

case_description: A man entered my house at night by breaking the door and took my jewelry.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Investigation and Prosecution Pursuant to Article 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Article 17(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

It is respectfully submitted that on the night of [date], the respondent trespassed into the house of the petitioner at [address] by means of force (Article 17(1) of BNSS), wherein he committed the offence of misappropriation of the petitioner's personal property, specifically jewelry, in contravention of Article 201(1) of the BNS.

The petitioner humbly requests that an investigation be conducted under Article 123(2) of the BNS to identify the respondent and secure evidence of the said offence, and that the respondent be prosecuted in accordance with Article 17(1) of the BNSS and Article 201(1) of the BNS.

Supporting documents and evidence are attached hereto.

Please accept this petition as a formal complaint.

Respectfully submitted,
[Petitioner's Name]

case_description: My neighbor keeps threatening to beat me if I use the common parking area.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 228(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Section 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I seek to know whether my neighbor's statements, threatening to cause bodily harm to me if I use the common parking area, constitute an offence under the BNS and if so, what are the applicable provisions and remedies available to me.

case_description: Two people started fighting on the street and one hit the other with a stick causing injuries.
rephrased_query:
**Incident Report and Legal Query**

**Case Description:** On [date], two individuals engaged in a physical altercation on a public street, resulting in one party inflicting grievous bodily harm upon the other using a stick.

**Legal Query:**

Pursuant to Article 304 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the actions of the accused constitute an offense under Chapter 10, Section 3, 'Causing Death or Grievous Hurt by a Hazardous Substance or an Instrument' or Chapter 16, Section 6, 'Voluntarily Causing Hurt' of the BNS? 

Further, under the provisions of Article 215 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what is the appropriate course of action for the investigating officer to take in securing the scene, collecting evidence, and recording statements from witnesses?

Additionally, in light of Article 123 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), how do the circumstances of the incident affect the admissibility of the physical evidence collected, particularly the stick used to inflict harm, and any other relevant documentation or testimony?

case_description: A person sent me abusive and vulgar messages repeatedly on WhatsApp.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 5, Section 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I submit the following formal legal query:

What constitutes a case of harassment under the provisions of BNS, specifically Article 15, Section 4, in relation to an individual sending repetitive abusive and vulgar messages on a digital platform, such as WhatsApp, and what penalties or remedies are available to the aggrieved party under BNSS, specifically Article 27, Section 6, for the commission of such offense?

case_description: Someone forged my signature on a cheque and withdrew money from my account.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Section 420 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), which deals with Cheating and Breach of Trust, I seek clarification on whether an offence under BNS has been committed by an individual who forged the signature on a cheque issued by me, thereby facilitating the withdrawal of funds from my account, thereby causing me financial loss.

Furthermore, under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and Article 110, I request guidance on the necessary procedures and protocols to be followed to lodge a complaint, investigate the case, and ensure the apprehension and prosecution of the perpetrator, as well as compensation for the damages suffered by me.

Additionally, under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I seek to understand the admissibility and relevance of the forged cheque as evidence in the trial, specifically under Article 32, which deals with the Proof of Signature.

Lastly, I request an assessment of the liability of any financial institution or bank involved in the transaction, under the provisions of BNS and BNSS.

case_description: My landlord locked me out of my rented room without any notice and kept my belongings inside.
rephrased_query:
Query:

Pursuant to Article 34, Clause 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), has the landlord committed the offence of wrongful confinement or illegal detention under Article 42, Section 1 of BNS, by locking out the tenant from the rented premises without lawful notice, thereby rendering the tenant unable to access their personal belongings as mentioned under Article 19, Section 5 of BNS? 

Additionally, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what procedures can be initiated under Chapter 3, Article 7, to secure the release of the tenant's belongings and ensure the landlord's compliance with the relevant laws?

case_description: A group of people damaged my shop during a protest by throwing stones and breaking the glass.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 43 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I submit the following formal complaint for consideration:

Whether the alleged perpetrators of the incident, involving intentional damage to property (specifically, a commercial establishment), by means of hurling projectiles (stones) and causing intentional destruction of glass panes, have committed the offence of "Mischief" under Section 43(1) of the BNS? 

Additionally, I request an investigation into the circumstances surrounding this incident, as mandated by Section 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), with a view to determining whether the perpetrators were acting in contravention of Sections 13 and 14 of the BNSS, which pertain to the maintenance of public order and the prevention of unlawful assemblies.

Furthermore, I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in relation to the identification of the perpetrators and the reconstruction of the events surrounding the incident, in light of Article 17(2) of the BSA, which deals with the admissibility of circumstantial evidence.

case_description: A stranger keeps calling and sending messages threatening to burn my shop if I do not pay him money.
rephrased_query:
Application of Section 306 of BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023) for alleged offences under Section 506 of BNS, seeking redress under Section 155 of BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) for protection and investigation.

Whether the facts presented constitute a prima facie case of extortion under Section 306 of BNS, justifying the initiation of a police investigation under Section 155 of BNSS and whether the complainant is entitled to protection under the said Act.

Further, this application seeks clarification on the admissibility of electronic evidence, including voice messages and SMS, as per Article 59 of BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023) for purposes of prosecution under Section 306 of BNS.

case_description: Someone hacked my social media account and posted offensive content using my name.
rephrased_query:
Complaint against Unauthorised Use of Personal Information and Defamation under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 123 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek your assistance in filing a complaint against an individual who has committed the offence of unauthorised use of personal information under Article 234(1)(a) of BNS, whereby my social media account was accessed without my consent, and offensive content was posted using my name.

Furthermore, under Article 219 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I also seek to file a complaint against the said individual for the offence of defamation, as the said content has caused harm to my reputation and goodwill.

Under Section 53(4) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that the investigation be conducted expeditiously, and the accused be brought to justice.

Pursuant to Article 17 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I submit the following documents as evidence:

* Screenshots of the offending posts
* Records of the social media account activity
* Testimony of witnesses who have seen the offending posts.

I request that the authorities take immediate action in this matter, investigate the circumstances surrounding the unauthorised use of my personal information and the posting of defamatory content, and bring the accused to justice in accordance with the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

case_description: During a land dispute my uncle stabbed my father multiple times with a knife and he died on the spot.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To whom it may concern,

I, [Your Name], son of the deceased, hereby lodge a complaint against my uncle, [Uncle's Name], for the alleged commission of the offence under BNS, Section 302 - Murder.

**Particulars of the Offence:**

On [date], at [place], my uncle, [Uncle's Name], with intent to kill, caused grievous hurt to my father by stabbing him multiple times with a knife. As a direct result of these injuries, my father succumbed to his injuries on the spot.

**Request for Investigation and Prosecution:**

I request that a thorough investigation be conducted under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and that my uncle be apprehended and prosecuted for the said offence. I also request that the evidence, including medical and forensic reports, be collected and preserved in accordance with the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

**Signature:**
[Your Signature]

**Date:**
[Date]

Please note that this is a formal complaint and may be used as evidence in any subsequent legal proceedings.

case_description: A man poured acid on a woman's face after she rejected his marriage proposal and she later succumbed to injuries.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), an inquiry is required to determine whether the accused has committed the offence of causing grievous hurt by an offender by means of poison, etc. (Article 315, BNS) and whether the said act was motivated by the victim's rejection of the accused's marriage proposal, thereby constituting the offence of dowry harassment or harassment with intent to coerce (Article 322, BNS).

Furthermore, an investigation is needed to ascertain whether the accused has committed the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, punishable under Article 302, BNS, and whether the victim's death was a direct consequence of the injuries inflicted upon her.

Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the inquiry and investigation should be conducted in accordance with the provisions related to the investigation of cognizable offences (Chapter VII, BNSS) and the provisions related to the investigation of non-cognizable offences (Chapter VIII, BNSS).

During the inquiry and investigation, the admissibility of evidence and the burden of proof should be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 21(1)(d), BSA, which deals with the burden of proof and the standard of proof in criminal cases.

case_description: My neighbor hit my brother on the head with an iron rod during a heated argument; he is in ICU and may not survive.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a complaint is hereby filed under the provisions of Section 299, BNS, read with Section 302, BNS, regarding an alleged offence of "Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder" (Section 306, BNS) and "Murder" (Section 307, BNS), committed by the neighbour against the brother. 

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, an application is made under Section 154, BNSS, to register an FIR (First Information Report) in this regard and to initiate an investigation into the said incident. 

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, we seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence in this case, specifically with regards to the provisions of Section 59, BSA, regarding the admissibility of statements made by the injured party (the brother) prior to his hospitalization, and Section 60, BSA, regarding the admissibility of medical evidence, including the hospital records of the brother.

case_description: Two men got into a drunken fight and one pushed the other off a bridge, causing his death.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Section 306 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

In the matter of the untimely demise of [Name of the deceased], who lost his life due to alleged culpable homicide, we seek clarification on the applicability of BNS Section 306, which pertains to culpable homicide not amounting to murder, particularly in scenarios involving reckless or negligent conduct. Specifically, we wish to understand whether the actions of the accused individual, who, in a state of intoxication, pushed the deceased off a bridge, resulting in his fatal fall, would constitute an offense under BNS Section 306.

Additionally, we request guidance on the procedural aspects of this matter, including the filing of the complaint, the initiation of an investigation, and the subsequent legal proceedings under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically Article 167, which deals with the procedure for investigating cognizable offenses.

Furthermore, we seek clarification on the admissibility of evidence under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with regard to the testimony of witnesses, the admissibility of statements made by the accused during the investigation, and the role of circumstantial evidence in establishing the guilt of the accused.

We kindly request the court's guidance on these matters, in order to ensure a thorough and fair investigation into the circumstances surrounding the deceased's untimely demise.

case_description: A bus driver was driving recklessly at high speed and ran over a pedestrian who died on the spot.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 45 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), in relation to Article 27, I request clarification on the liability of the bus driver under the provisions of 'Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder' for causing the death of the pedestrian, arising out of his alleged 'Reckless Driving' in contravention of Article 32 of the BNS, and whether the offense falls within the definition of 'Cognizable Offense' as per Article 56 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), thus necessitating registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Article 20 of the BNSS.

case_description: A wife was continuously tortured by her husband and in-laws for dowry; she was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage.
rephrased_query:
**INQUIRY INTO CIRCUMSTANCES SURROUNDING THE DEATH OF A FEMALE**

Pursuant to Section 176(1)(g) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a complaint is made against the husband and in-laws of the deceased for alleged commission of the offence under Section 312(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), read with Sections 312(2) and 312(3) thereof, arising out of the continuous harassment and torture inflicted upon the deceased by the accused.

The circumstances of the case, including the fact that the deceased was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage, necessitate an investigation to ascertain whether the death was caused by the accused's acts constituting the aforesaid offence.

The prosecution is required to prove the guilt of the accused under Section 101(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), which provides that the burden of proving the defence of the accused lies on them. Consequently, the accused must establish that their actions did not constitute the aforesaid offence or that they were not responsible for the death of the deceased.

The court is required to inquire into the circumstances surrounding the death and to determine whether the accused are guilty of the offence alleged against them, in accordance with the principles of natural justice and the provisions of the BNSS and the BNS.

case_description: A teenager posted on social media encouraging her classmate to commit suicide; the classmate later took her own life.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)**

**Query:** A case is reported where a minor, vide a social media post, allegedly incited her classmate to take her own life, which subsequently led to the classmate's demise. 

**Question:**

1. **Offence under BNS:** Can the minor be held liable for abetment of suicide under Article 302(1)(a) of BNS, given that her actions allegedly led to the classmate's death? 
2. **Investigation under BNSS:** What provisions of BNSS (Articles 54, 55, and 56) govern the investigation into this incident, particularly in relation to the minor's social media post and its probable impact on the classmate?
3. **Evidence collection under BSA:** What sections of BSA (Articles 17, 28, 29, and 31) would be applicable in collecting and preserving evidence related to the social media post, online activities, and other relevant data in this case?
4. **Proceedings and Trial under BNSS:** What is the procedure under BNSS (Articles 80, 81, and 82) for conducting the trial, considering the minor's age, and ensuring that justice is served in a fair and compassionate manner?

**Request:** In light of BNS, BNSS, and BSA, kindly provide guidance on the applicable laws, procedures, and any relevant precedents that may be cited in this case.

case_description: A life-convict on parole got into a fight and strangled another person to death.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 302 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the act of the life-convict on parole resulting in the death of another person through strangulation constitutes an offence under Section 302, and whether such act would amount to 'murder' under the said provision, thereby attracting the prescribed punishment. 

Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, what are the necessary steps to be taken by the authorities in this regard, particularly in regards to Article 167 (arrest) and Article 168 (custody) of the said Code, considering the life-convict's status of being on parole at the time of the incident.

case_description: A man fired his licensed gun at his business partner during a heated dispute but the bullet missed narrowly.
rephrased_query:
**Case Query:**

Pursuant to Article 302(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is alleged that the accused committed an act of attempted murder under Chapter V, Section 301(B) of the BNS, by discharging a firearm at his business partner, thereby endangering his life, albeit narrowly missing the target.

**Further Inquiries:**

1. **Article 13(2) of the BNSS:** Did the accused obtain valid permission to carry the firearm, as per the Arms Act, and whether such permit was valid at the time of the incident?
2. **Article 20(1) of the BNSS:** Was the accused aware that his actions may lead to harm to another person, particularly his business partner, during the heated dispute?
3. **Section 5(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA):** Is there any direct evidence, such as eyewitness accounts, video footage, or physical evidence, to establish the sequence of events leading to the alleged crime?
4. **Article 17(2) of the BNSS:** Did the accused's actions constitute a breach of peace and public order, thereby warranting investigation under the provisions of the BNSS?

case_description: A cook mixed rat poison into the food served at a party and three guests died after consuming it.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, what would be the penal consequences under Section 304A for the cook who, with the intention of causing harm, mixed rat poison into the food served at a party and caused the death of three guests?

Furthermore, under Article 22(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, would the cook be considered a "culpable homicide not amounting to murder" under Section 299, and if so, what would be the relevant provisions of Article 14(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 that would govern the investigation and prosecution of this case?

Additionally, under Article 15(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what would be the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly with regards to the testimony of the cook and any other witnesses who may have observed the cook mixing the rat poison into the food, in light of Article 25(2) and Article 27(1) of the said Act?

case_description: My 8-year-old son was taken away by unknown persons from outside his school and we received a ransom call demanding ten lakh rupees.
rephrased_query:
Petition under Article 12 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), seeking registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 3(1) of BNSS in relation to the alleged commission of the offence of Kidnapping for Ransom, punishable under Article 21 of BNS, and requesting immediate investigation and rescue of the child.

Specifically, the petition seeks to invoke the provisions of Section 2(3) of BNSS for the purpose of expeditious and fair investigation, and to obtain necessary assistance and cooperation from the authorities under Article 18 of BNS for the safe recovery of the child. 

Additionally, the petition requests the Court to direct the Investigating Officer to gather evidence and collect statements from witnesses under the provisions of Article 25 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) and to submit a detailed report under Article 13 of BNS.

case_description: A young woman was lured with a fake job offer and trafficked to another state where she was forced into prostitution.
rephrased_query:
Notified to the concerned authorities under Section 4(B) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a complaint is hereby lodged regarding an alleged offence under Section 4(A)(i) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - 'Exploitation of Vulnerable Person through False Promise', read with Section 6(A)(iii) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - 'Conspiracy to Traffic Person for Commercial Sexual Exploitation'. The incident allegedly occurred as a result of an offence under Section 7(B)(ii) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - 'Forcing a Person into Commercial Sexual Exploitation'. 

Pursuant to Section 22(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, it is requested that a magisterial inquiry be conducted into the matter and necessary action be taken under Section 28(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 to safeguard the rights of the victim. 

In accordance with Section 15(A)(i) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, it is requested to obtain and preserve evidence related to the offence, including any electronic communication, documents or other materials relevant to the case, and to examine the victim as a witness under Section 19(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

case_description: A gang kidnapped children from railway stations and maimed them to use for organized begging.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Section 302, 369, and 342 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To Whom It May Concern,

I lodge a complaint against a gang involved in the commission of the following crimes:

**Crime 1: Abduction and Maiming**

The group has been abducting children from railway stations and inflicting grievous injuries upon them, thereby causing them severe physical harm. This act constitutes the offense of causing the death and grievous hurt under Article 302 of the BNS (Causing death by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide), Article 369 of the BNS (Kidnapping from lawful guardianship), and Article 342 of the BNS (Voluntarily causing grievous hurt).

**Crime 2: Exploitation**

The accused gang is using the abducted and maimed children for organized begging, which is an act of exploitation. This offense falls under Article __________ of the BNS (to be specified after further research).

**Request**

I request you to register a First Information Report (FIR) under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and to investigate this case under the provisions of the BNSS.

**Evidence**

I request the investigating officer to collect evidence in accordance with Article 25 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), including but not limited to:

- Statements of witnesses under Section 17 of the BSA
- Documentary evidence under Section 18 of the BSA
- Physical evidence under Section 19 of the BSA
- Medical evidence under Section 20 of the BSA

I request you to take necessary action in this matter, and I am willing to cooperate with the investigation.

**Signature**

[Your Signature]

**Date**

[Date]

case_description: My teenage daughter was taken away by a man she met online without my knowledge or consent.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 12(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I request to report an alleged commission of the offence of "Abduction of a Minor" and/or "Kidnapping" as defined in Article 18(2)(c) of BNS, in contravention of Article 19(3)(a) of BNSS, which mandates the reporting of missing persons.

Noting that the victim is a minor, I request an investigation into this incident under Article 20(1)(i) of BNSS, ensuring the preservation of evidence and the protection of the rights of the minor as an informant under Article 21(4)(b) of BNSS.

Further, I request an examination of the online interactions between the victim and the alleged perpetrator, in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with respect to the admissibility of digital evidence under Article 35(2)(d) of BSA, and the reliability of online testimony as per Article 42(1)(a) of BSA.

I request the authorities to take necessary measures to locate and secure the safe return of the minor, and to initiate proceedings against the alleged perpetrator as per Article 28(1)(c) of BNSS.

case_description: An auto-rickshaw driver forcibly took a woman passenger to an isolated area against her will.
rephrased_query:
Petition for the Enforcement of Protection of Personal Liberty and Prevention of Unlawful Restraint and Confinement under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Whether the actions of the auto-rickshaw driver, as described, constitute an offence punishable under Article 321 (1)(a) of the BNS (Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder) or Article 321 (1)(c) BNS (Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means) since these actions have not been specified and whether they fall under the provisions of Article 321(1)(h) of the BNS (Sexual Assault), or Article 321 (1)(j) of the BNS (Kidnapping or Abduction) and/or Article 321 (1)(g) of the BNS (Unlawful Restraint) of a woman passenger against her will.

Whether the police have a duty to register an FIR under Article 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and to conduct a thorough investigation into this incident.

Whether the prosecution can rely on circumstantial evidence as per Article 59(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for conviction of the accused and the admissibility of digital evidence under Article 54 of the BSA.

Whether the accused can be held criminally liable under Article 21(7) of the BNS and the provision of anticipatory bail under Article 34 of the BNSS in light of these circumstances.

case_description: A child under ten was stolen from her parents at a mela and later found being sold to a couple in another city.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 12, Subsection 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek clarification on the applicability of Section 315A(1) of the BNS in relation to the alleged abduction of a minor child under ten years of age, in contravention of Article 316(2)(i) of the BNS, at a public gathering (mela). Furthermore, we seek guidance on whether the subsequent sale of the child to a couple in another city constitutes an offence under Section 318(2) of the BNS, thereby triggering the mandatory reporting requirements under Article 320(4) of the BNS, as amended by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Please note that the relevant evidence collected by the investigating authorities should be examined in light of the provisions of Article 41, Subsection 1 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically the burden of proof as per Article 42(3) of the BSA, to determine the culpability of the accused individuals.

case_description: A factory owner brought migrant workers from Bihar with false promises and made them work without pay under locked conditions.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), this office seeks clarification on the applicability of Section 117(1) of BNS, relating to "Exploitation of Labour" and Article 10(3) of the BNS, which defines "Cruel and Inhuman Treatment". 

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), we seek guidance on the appropriate sections for registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 3(1) of BNSS, in relation to the alleged contravention of Sections 23(2) and 24(1) of BNS, which deal with "False Promises" and "Confinement for Labour", respectively.

Lastly, in conformity with the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), we request an interpretation on the admissibility of evidence under Section 59(1) of BSA, in relation to the statements made by the migrant workers, as protected under Article 26(2) of BSA, which deals with "Protection of Accused Persons".

case_description: A man kidnapped his ex-wife's 6-year-old child from her home and fled to a different state.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023), it is respectfully requested to clarify the following:

Whether the alleged act of the man, constituting the unlawful taking away or confinement of a child (hereinafter referred to as the "minor") from the lawful custody of its mother, constitutes the offence of "Child Kidnapping" under BNS, Article 321(1)?

Further, whether the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) provisions for "Transfer of Proceedings in Certain Cases" under Section 32(2) would be applicable in this scenario, considering the man fled to a different state with the minor?

Additionally, what would be the admissibility of evidence in this case, in light of BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023) provisions on "Presumption as to Certain Facts" under Section 13(3), particularly with regard to the identification of the minor and the chain of custody of the minor during the alleged kidnapping?

case_description: Several girls from a village were promised nursing jobs abroad but were taken to a city and forced into the flesh trade.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a formal complaint is being registered against the accused individuals for their involvement in the alleged commission of a cognizable offence under Section 3(1)(a) of BNS, read with Section 4(2)(i) of BNS, for engaging in human trafficking and forced prostitution. The incident allegedly occurred in a city, where the victims were subjected to coercion and exploitation by the accused, thereby violating their fundamental rights and freedoms under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

In view of the circumstances, it is requested to invoke the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically Section 15(1)(b) of BNSS, to authorize the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) and to initiate an investigation under the supervision of a Magistrate, as per Article 50 of BNSS.

Further, it is prayed that the investigating officer may be directed to collect evidence, including documentary and testimonial evidence, in accordance with the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 13 of BSA, to establish the guilt of the accused and to bring them to justice.

case_description: A couple bought a 4-year-old boy from an orphanage caretaker who had no authority to sell children.
rephrased_query:
Subject: Inquiry into Alleged Offence of Unlawful Child Trafficking and Unauthorised Transfer of Custody.

To Whom It May Concern,

Pursuant to Article 10(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I request clarification on the following incident:

A couple procured a 4-year-old boy from the caretaker of an orphanage, notwithstanding the caretaker's express lack of authority to transfer custody of the child. The circumstances raise concerns regarding potential contravention of Article 21(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and Section 8 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, which pertains to the protection of vulnerable individuals, including minors.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence in the event that the caretaker asserts a colourable defence of ignorance regarding the illegality of the transaction.

Please provide your expert opinion on the applicable BNS and BNSS provisions, as well as the relevant BSA guidelines for assessing the validity of the couple's claim.

Yours faithfully,
[Your Name]

case_description: Three men on a motorcycle snatched my gold chain while I was walking on the road and one of them showed a knife.
rephrased_query:
In light of the recent amendments to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I respectfully submit the following formal legal query:

Pursuant to Article 322(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I request investigation and prosecution of the aforementioned incident under the provisions governing theft and robbery. Specifically, I seek to invoke Article 154 of the BNS, which pertains to the offense of "dishonestly receiving stolen property", in conjunction with Article 156, which deals with the offense of "robbery".

I also request that the accused be charged under Article 378(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which concerns the offense of "assault or use of criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of duty", as one of the perpetrators allegedly displayed a knife during the commission of the offense.

Furthermore, I request that the prosecution take into account the provisions of Article 13(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, which deals with the admissibility of evidence, particularly with regards to the testimony of eyewitnesses, in order to gather evidence and build a strong case against the accused.

Finally, I request that the investigation be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 102(1), which outlines the procedure for registration of FIR and investigation of cognizable offenses.

case_description: A gang of seven armed men broke into a jewellery shop at night, tied up the watchman, and looted all the gold and cash.
rephrased_query:
Query: 
Pursuant to Article 43, Clause 1 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the actions of the seven armed men constitute the offence of "Dacoity" under Article 174, Clause 2, and if so, what are the relevant provisions of Article 43, Clause 1 for the determination of their liability, considering that they employed force or threat to gain entry and committed a breach of peaceful possession of the jeweller's shop, as per Article 43, Clause 2.

Additionally, under Article 56, Clause 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, whether the police have the authority to conduct an investigation and, if necessary, arrest the perpetrators without a warrant, given the circumstances of the breach of the peace and commission of dacoity, in accordance with Article 56, Clause 5.

Lastly, under Article 81, Clause 1 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what is the burden of proof that the prosecutor must establish to secure a conviction against the accused, and whether the testimony of the watchman, as a witness, will suffice to establish the chain of events, in accordance with Article 81, Clause 2.

case_description: A local goon demands monthly protection money from shopkeepers in my area and beats those who refuse to pay.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 302 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a formal complaint is hereby lodged against an individual who has been allegedly engaged in extortion and causing hurt to those who refused to comply with their demands, by virtue of Section 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

The complainant seeks to know whether the aforesaid acts constitute an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and, if so, what are the necessary steps to be taken for the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

Additionally, the complainant requests clarification on the admissibility of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, particularly with respect to Section 13, which deals with the recording of statements by the police, and Section 20, which pertains to the admissibility of circumstantial evidence.

The complainant also wishes to know whether the accused can be held liable under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 for the act of extortion and causing hurt, and if so, what are the possible punishments that may be imposed upon them, as per Article 405 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

case_description: While returning from an ATM at night, two people held me at gunpoint and took away all my cash and debit card.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Registration of a Crime under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Investigation under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) - 

To Whom It May Concern,

I submit a complaint of dacoity (Article 321, BNS) that occurred on the night of [date], during which I was robbed of a substantial amount of cash and a debit card at gunpoint by two unidentified individuals near the ATM. The perpetrators restrained me against my will, thereby committing an act of physical restraint and confinement (Article 312, BNS).

I request that the relevant authorities under the BNSS immediately register a First Information Report (FIR) in this matter and initiate a detailed investigation. I request that the investigation proceedings be conducted in accordance with Articles 43 and 45 of the BNSS, which mandate the collection of evidence and the apprehension of the offenders.

I further request that the investigation be conducted under the supervision of the Magistrate (Article 91, BNSS) and that all necessary steps be taken to ensure my safety and well-being during the pendency of the investigation.

I request that the evidence collected during the investigation be examined in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly Section 19 thereof, which deals with the admissibility of digital evidence.

I request that the investigation be concluded at the earliest and that the perpetrators be brought to justice.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

[Your Signature]
[Your Name]

case_description: A group of dacoits attacked a village, looted houses, and assaulted several villagers causing serious injuries.
offense_category: dacoity with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 121 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), the complainant seeks an investigation into the alleged commission of the offence under Article 147(1) of BNS, specifically the crime of "Dacoity" and its related consequences, as per BNS Section 2(i) and Section 2(k), and Article 147(2). The complainant further seeks action under Article 148 of BNS for "Assault with intent to cause grievous hurt" as per BNS Section 2(m) in relation to the injuries sustained by the villagers. Please refer to Article 149 of BNS for further clarification on "Causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means" and Article 150 of BNS in relation to "Voluntarily causing grievous hurt" as a result of the assault.

Considering the situation, the complainant also requests that the investigation be conducted under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the protection of the complainant's rights and the rights of the victims, and that the police take necessary precautions under BNSS Article 20 to secure the scene of the crime and preserve evidence.

Additionally, the complainant seeks evidence regarding the identity of the perpetrators under Article 34 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) and requests that all relevant witnesses be examined under BSA Article 35 to ascertain their roles and involvement in the alleged crimes.

case_description: Someone showed me a knife in a train and forcibly took my laptop bag and wallet.
rephrased_query:
I, [Name], being a victim of the aforesaid incident, hereby submit the following formal complaint:

Is the accused liable under Section 304 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for the wrongful seizure of my personal property (laptop bag and wallet) through the use of coercion in a public place (train), which may also constitute an act of criminal intimidation?

Furthermore, can the accused be held responsible under Article 3 (1) (b) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for failure to prevent or report the commission of a cognizable offense, namely, the wrongful seizure of my property and potential threat to my safety?

Additionally, I request guidance on whether the accused's actions, which involved the display of a knife, would constitute sufficient proof under Section 2 (15) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to establish a prima facie case against them for the aforementioned offenses?

case_description: A person claiming to be a police officer stopped my car, showed a fake ID, and demanded cash to let me go without a 'challan'.
offense_category: extortion by impersonation of public servant
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

Whether Section 12 (Impersonation) of BNS is made out in the instant case, where a person, who falsely claimed to be a public servant, i.e., a police officer (Article 2, Definitions of BNS), used a forged document (Article 13, Definition of 'forged document') to establish his authority, and demanded an unlawful gratification (Section 15, Extortion) in exchange for not issuing a legal notice (Article 3, Definitions of BNS) to the complainant.

**Complaint under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)**

Can a police officer's dereliction of duty, as alleged in the instant case, be considered a breach of duty under BNSS, warranting registration of an FIR under Section 17 (Failure to perform duties) and action under Article 23 (Duty to perform and observe the laws of the land)?

**Complaint under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA)**

Whether the accused's actions, as described, amount to an attempt to procure a false document (Section 20, Falsification of evidence) or to fabricate a false document (Section 21, Fabrication of false evidence), which would be a violation of Article 18 (Definition of 'evidence') and/or Section 22 (Fabrication of false evidence) of BSA?

case_description: Armed robbers hijacked a delivery truck on the highway, tied the driver, and stole the entire consignment of electronics.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123 (1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is respectfully submitted that:

Whether the perpetrators of the armed robbery, who hijacked a delivery truck on the highway, tied the driver, and stole the entire consignment of electronics, have committed the offense of "Dacoity" under Article 224 of BNS, which attracts the punishment under Article 227 of BNS?

Further, it is requested to examine the applicability of Article 235 of BNS, specifically the offense of "Criminal Intimidation" in this case.

Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what are the procedures to be followed in order to register an FIR (First Information Report) in this matter, and what are the steps to be taken by the law enforcement authorities under Article 12 of BNSS to initiate an investigation?

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what is the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly with regards to the electronic devices stolen, and the statements made by the driver who was tied during the hijacking?

case_description: My servant stole cash and gold ornaments from my almirah using a duplicate key he had secretly made.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Investigation and Prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

I, the complainant, submit this petition, praying that an investigation be initiated under Article 12 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against my servant, who has committed the offence of theft by secretly making a duplicate key and using it to steal cash and gold ornaments from my almirah, in contravention of Article 174 (1) of the same Act.

I pray that the Magistrate may direct the registration of an FIR under Article 20 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and authorise the investigator to collect evidence, including documentary and physical evidence, as per Article 30 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), to establish the guilt of the accused.

I request that the Magistrate may also direct the accused to be produced before the Court, and the case be tried in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Verification Certificate from the Police Station: [Insert]

Verification Certificate from the Public Prosecutor: [Insert]

Signature of the Complainant: [Insert]

Date: [Insert]

case_description: A known criminal gang has been robbing buses on rural roads; they stop the bus, beat passengers, and take all valuables.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Investigation and Prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

Whether the actions of the known criminal gang amount to the commission of offence(s) under Chapter III, "Offences Against Persons" and Chapter V, "Offences Against Property" of the BNS, specifically Article 12(1)(a) ("Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder") in conjunction with Article 13(2)(b) ("Voluntarily causing hurt") and Article 20(1)(a) ("Theft") and/or Article 25(1)(a) ("Dacoity").

Whether the said actions also amount to an obstruction of public service under Article 32(1)(b) of the BNSS, specifically Article 34(4)(a) ("Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant").

Pursuant to Article 41(3) of the BNSS, whether the investigating agency should initiate an inquiry and gather evidence in accordance with Chapter VII, "Investigation" of the BNSS, including the collection of physical evidence and witness statements.

Whether the collected evidence can be used as admissible evidence under Chapter IX, "Evidence" of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 23(2)(a) ("Relevant fact") and Article 31(1)(b) ("Motive, preparation, and knowledge").

case_description: A real-estate agent collected advance money for a flat that he had already sold to someone else.
rephrased_query:
Whether the actions of the real-estate agent amount to the offence of 'dishonest misappropriation of property' under Article 266 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), and whether the said agent can be prosecuted under Article 267 of the BNS for 'criminal breach of trust', given that he collected advance money with the intention of using it for his personal gain. 

Additionally, whether the said real-estate agent can be arrested and investigated under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), and whether any evidence collected during the investigation would be admissible under Article 24 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) as relevant to the case.

What is the admissibility of any documentary evidence, such as receipts or bank statements, as proof of the real-estate agent's wrongful actions under Article 25 of the BSA, and what is the procedure for examining such evidence under Article 26 of the BSA.

case_description: An accountant in our company siphoned off funds by creating fake invoices and transferring money to his personal account.
offense_category: criminal breach of trust and falsification of accounts
rephrased_query:
PETITION FOR INVESTIGATION AND PROSECUTION UNDER BNS AND BNSS

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

Subsequent to receiving information regarding an alleged incident of misappropriation of company funds by an accountant, it is respectfully submitted that:

* The accused, in his capacity as an accountant, is suspected of having committed an offence under Article 123(1)(d) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) by dishonestly misappropriating company funds.
* The accused allegedly created fake invoices and utilized them to facilitate the unauthorized transfer of company funds to his personal account, thereby causing loss to the company.
* We respectfully request that you initiate an inquiry under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to gather evidence and investigate the circumstances surrounding this incident.
* We pray that upon completion of the inquiry, you proceed to prosecute the accused under Article 123(1)(d) of the BNS and Article 28 of the BNSS, as applicable.
* We also request that you consider issuing summons to the accused under Article 20 of the BNSS to appear before the court and answer to the allegations leveled against him.
* We further request that you direct the accused to produce all relevant records and documents related to the company's financial transactions during the period in question.

Please find attached the supporting documents and evidence in relation to this matter.

Yours faithfully,

[Your Name]
[Your Designation]
[Your Address]
[Your Contact Information]

case_description: I purchased a used car online; the seller provided forged RC and insurance documents and the car turned out to be stolen.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I request clarification on the applicable penal provisions for the offence committed by the seller in furnishing false documents, particularly Article 173(2)(b) of the BNS, which appears to be relevant in this scenario.

Furthermore, under Article 56 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I seek guidance on the procedures to be followed for registering a complaint and initiating an investigation against the seller, specifically regarding the seizure of the forged documents and the stolen vehicle.

Additionally, pursuant to Article 27(5) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I request clarification on the admissibility of electronic records, including email communications and online transaction records, as evidence in this case, particularly in relation to the seller's intent and knowledge of the vehicle's true ownership status.

case_description: A courier agent collected valuables for delivery but never delivered them and switched off his phone.
rephrased_query:
Complaint under Section 414 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (theft by carrier) is warranted. 

It is submitted that an individual, purportedly a courier agent, did receive valuables for delivery with the intent to deliver them. However, the said individual has failed to deliver the valuables and has switched off his mobile phone, thereby making himself unavailable for communication.

Pursuant to Section 102 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, the police may take cognizance of this offense and initiate an investigation.

As per Section 8 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, the burden of proof to establish that the valuables were received by the courier agent for delivery and that he has failed to deliver them lies on the complainant.

case_description: A man called my elderly mother pretending to be a bank officer and got her to share OTP; Rs 2 lakh was withdrawn from her account.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek an explanation for the alleged commission of the offence under Article 379 (1) (a) BNS, wherein a person impersonating a public servant allegedly induced the victim, an elderly woman, to part with her personal information including an OTP, thereby facilitating the unauthorized withdrawal of Rs 2 lakh from her bank account. 

Furthermore, I request clarification under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) regarding the procedures to be followed for registering a First Information Report (FIR) under Article 154 (2) (a) BNSS, and to obtain necessary police protection and compensation for the victim, in accordance with the provisions of Article 210 (4) BNSS.

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I seek guidance on the admissibility of electronic evidence, specifically the OTP and transaction records, as per Article 57 (3) (c) BSA, and the burden of proof that may be placed on the accused in establishing the authenticity of the transaction.

case_description: My business partner secretly transferred company funds to his personal account and denied any knowledge of it.
rephrased_query:
Query for Legal Advice: 

Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, the question arises whether the actions of a business partner, who secretly transferred company funds to his personal bank account without the knowledge or consent of the other stakeholders, constitute an offence under Article 265 (dishonest misappropriation of property), Article 267 (misappropriation of entrusted property), or Article 278 (fraudulent dealing in property) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

Further, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, what are the procedures to be followed for registering a complaint and conducting an investigation in this regard, especially considering the provisions related to offences by companies, criminal conspiracy, and the rights of victims.

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what are the admissible forms of evidence to prove the business partner's knowledge and complicity in the said transaction, and the procedures to be followed for the collection, preservation, and production of documentary and other forms of evidence in this case?

case_description: A fake charity collected donations from the public for flood relief but used all the money for personal expenses.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is submitted that:

Whether the accused, having collected donations from the public for charitable purposes under the guise of flood relief, committed the offence of fraudulently misappropriating funds under Article 266 of the BNS and Section 13 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, thereby cheating and dishonestly inducing the public to part with their property in contravention of Article 267 of the BNS.

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is requested to determine whether the accused's actions constitutes a cognizable offence under Section 2(1)(b) of the BNSS, warranting their arrest and investigation under Section 3 of the BNSS.

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is submitted to enquire into the admissibility of evidence, including bank statements, receipts, and witness testimony, in establishing the guilt of the accused under Article 21 of the BSA.

case_description: A jeweller replaced my real diamond with a fake one during a repair and returned the fake stone claiming it was mine.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Redress under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS):

Against: [Jeweller's Name] 
Complainant: [Your Name]

The complainant alleges that the respondent, [Jeweller's Name], perpetrated an offence under Article 265(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), by dishonestly replacing the complainant's genuine diamond with a counterfeit one, resulting in the complainant suffering pecuniary loss.

Prayer: The respondent be directed to return the complainant's original diamond and pay compensation as per Article 265(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), and be proceeded against under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for the aforesaid offence.

Petition under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), for the following reliefs:

1. To direct the respondent to produce the original diamond before the Magistrate within a period of 7 days from the date of this petition, as per Article 25(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).
2. To direct the respondent to pay a sum of Rs. [amount] as compensation to the complainant within a period of 30 days from the date of this order, as per Article 45(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).
3. To direct the respondent to execute a personal bond with 2 sureties, as per Article 75(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), to the effect that they shall not repeat the offence in future.

Relevant Evidence: The complainant requests the court to admit the following documents as evidence under Article 120 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA):
- A detailed description of the original diamond, including its serial number and certification from a recognized gemological laboratory.
- A receipt for the repair of the diamond, indicating that the respondent had possession of the original diamond.
- A statement from the complainant detailing the events leading to the alleged offence.
- Photographic evidence of the original diamond and the counterfeit diamond.

The complainant requests that the court summon the respondent to appear before it and produce the original diamond, as required under Article 25(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

case_description: I paid a travel agent Rs 3 lakh for a holiday package but no bookings were ever made and he is now unreachable.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 17(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested to examine whether the travel agent has committed the offence of cheating by personation, as defined under Chapter 11, Section 3 of BNS, and to investigate the circumstances surrounding the non-execution of the holiday package bookings for which payment of Rs 3 lakh was made.

Further, under Article 42(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is requested that a First Information Report (FIR) be registered against the travel agent under the relevant provisions of BNSS, and that necessary steps be taken to bring the individual to justice.

Additionally, under Section 4 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is requested that all relevant documents, including receipts, invoices, and communication records, be collected and preserved as evidence in connection with this matter.

case_description: A builder collected money from twenty buyers for the same ten flats by showing forged allotment letters.
rephrased_query: Petition for redressal of grievances under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically Section 321 (Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property) and/or Section 424 (dishonestly or fraudulently removing or concealing property) - seeking an investigation and prosecution of the builder for allegedly collecting monies from twenty buyers under false pretenses and presenting forged allotment letters, and enjoining interim measures pending the outcome of the proceedings under the aegis of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, Article 102 (Protection of interest of victims of crime).

case_description: A person published a false article in the newspaper accusing me of corruption without any evidence, damaging my reputation.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 45(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I submit the following formal complaint:

"Whether the act of publishing a false article in the newspaper, which accused the complainant of corruption without any evidence, constitutes an offence under Article 23(2)(a) of the BNS, thereby causing harm to the complainant's reputation as per Article 19(2)(b) of the BNS?

Furthermore, I pray that under Article 35 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the court may direct the publication to provide the evidence supporting the allegations made against the complainant, and if no evidence is forthcoming, to take necessary steps to restore the complainant's reputation as per Article 37(1) of the BNSS.

Additionally, under Article 27 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I request the court to consider the burden of proof and the onus of establishing the truth of the allegations made against the complainant, as well as the admissibility of any evidence that may be produced by the publication to support its claims."

Signed,
[Your Name]

case_description: A factory in our residential area releases toxic fumes every night causing breathing problems for all the residents.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint for Offence under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To the Honourable Magistrate,

Pursuant to Article 12(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I submit this complaint against the factory in our residential area for causing harm to public health and environment.

**Facts of the Case:**

On numerous occasions, the factory has been releasing toxic fumes every night, resulting in breathing problems for all the residents of our area. The fumes have been causing significant discomfort, distress, and health issues, thereby affecting our quality of life.

**Offences Alleged:**

The factory is liable for committing the offence of 'Causing Harm to Public Health' under Article 21(3)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which prohibits any activity that endangers the health or safety of the public.

**Relief Sought:**

I request the Honourable Magistrate to take immediate action against the factory and to direct the authorities to take necessary steps to prevent the release of toxic fumes from the factory and to compensate the residents for the harm caused.

**Evidence:**

I am willing to provide any additional evidence or testimony in support of this complaint, as required by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

**Request for Investigation:**

I respectfully request the Honourable Magistrate to direct the police to conduct a thorough investigation into this matter, as per Article 27(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and to take necessary steps to bring the perpetrators to justice.

Thank you.

**Your Name**
**Your Address**

case_description: Someone is running an illegal lottery office in our neighborhood and many people have lost money.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Perpetual Injunction and Compensation under Article 420 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Sections 102(1), 132, 133 and 136 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

It is respectfully submitted that the respondent is operating an illegal lottery office in our neighborhood, thereby committing the offence of cheating and fraud under Article 420 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

Furthermore, the respondent's actions have resulted in numerous individuals losing significant sums of money, thereby causing them irreparable harm and financial loss. We pray that the Hon'ble Magistrate may take cognizance of this matter under Section 102(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and direct the respondent to cease and desist from such activities forthwith.

We also pray that the respondent be held liable for the losses suffered by the victims and be directed to pay compensation as per the provisions of Article 420 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Section 133 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Pursuant to Section 136 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), we pray that the Magistrate may also issue a perpetual injunction restraining the respondent from operating any lottery office or engaging in any similar activities in the future.

We request that the Hon'ble Magistrate may hear this matter at the earliest and take appropriate action under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Respectfully submitted,
[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[Your Contact Information]

(Note: The formal legal query is written in a way that seeks a perpetual injunction and compensation from the respondent under the new laws. The actual legal process and terminology may vary depending on the specific circumstances and the jurisdiction.)

case_description: A person was singing obscene songs and making vulgar gestures in a public park in front of women and children.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek clarification on the applicability of Section 294A (Public Breaches of Decency in Public Places) in relation to the aforementioned incident.

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I would like to know the procedure to be followed in arresting, detaining, and prosecuting the accused, specifically in light of Articles 39-41 of the BNSS, which govern the apprehension, examination, and remand of an accused person.

Additionally, considering the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I request guidance on the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly with respect to the testimony of witnesses who were present at the scene, as governed by Article 13 of the BSA, which deals with the testimonial competence of witnesses.

case_description: My ex-boyfriend shared my private photographs on social media and created a fake profile using my pictures.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 228(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested to clarify whether the act of ex-boyfriend sharing complainant's private photographs on social media without her consent constitutes an offence under Section 19 of the BNS, specifically, disclosure of private information without consent, and whether the creation of a fake profile using the complainant's pictures amounts to 'Identity Theft' under Section 29 of the BNS, thereby warranting further investigation and potential prosecution under the aforesaid provisions of BNS.

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is requested to guide on the procedural aspects of investigating this complaint, particularly in relation to the procedures laid down under Chapter VII of the BNSS for the collection and preservation of evidence, including digital evidence, as per Article 118 of the BNSS.

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is requested to clarify whether the photographs and information on the fake profile shall be considered as relevant evidence under Section 5 of the BSA and whether the complainant's private messages or other electronic communications shall be admissible as evidence under Section 23 of the BSA, particularly in light of Article 30 of the BSA, which deals with the admissibility of digital records.

case_description: A shop is openly selling obscene magazines and DVDs to school children near a school campus.
offense_category: sale of obscene material to children
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 67(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is respectfully submitted that the following incident requires investigation and potential prosecution: 

A shop is allegedly selling material deemed to be obscene and indecent pursuant to Article 123(1)(d) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), which is being openly displayed and sold to school children near a school campus, thereby endangering the well-being and moral development of minors as per Article 15(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) in conjunction with BNSS provisions regarding protection of children from harm.

In order to establish the facts, the following questions are posed:

1. Whether the material sold by the shop constitutes obscene and indecent content as defined in Article 123(1)(d) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)?
2. Whether the shop owner or manager has knowledge of or was reckless in relation to the sale of such material to school children?
3. Whether the shop's actions constitute a criminal offense under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), and if so, what is the appropriate penalty?

In light of the above, a thorough investigation is required to determine the facts and apply the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

case_description: A man standing on the road deliberately shows obscene images on his phone to women passing by.
rephrased_query:
To: The Commissioner of Police, [District/State]
Subject: Request for Investigation and Prosecution under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023

Pursuant to Article 293 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a complaint is made against an individual who has allegedly committed an act of public nuisance by deliberately displaying obscene images on his mobile phone to women passing by on the road.

The query seeks an investigation and potential prosecution under Article 293 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which states:

"Whoever, in any public place, intentionally displays any obscene image or material, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both."

Further, it is requested to examine the application of Article 35 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for the purposes of arresting and detaining the accused, as it states:

"...the police officer may, without an order from a Magistrate and under a law, arrest any person who commits, or attempts to commit, a cognizable offence..."

Additionally, the query seeks guidance on the admissibility of electronic evidence under Article 17 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, which states:

"...electronic records and documents may be used as evidence, if they are properly certified and authenticated, and if they are found to be reliable and trustworthy..."

case_description: A woman was raped by a man who broke into her house late at night when she was alone.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), the complainant seeks an inquiry into the alleged commission of the offence under Article 321 (Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder or Rape) read with Article 323 (Sexual Assault) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), by the accused, who is alleged to have committed an act of Article 323 (Sexual Assault) by breaking into the complainant's residence at night, in contravention of Article 411 (House-Trespass after Preparation for Hurt, Assault or Theft) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), and thereby allegedly causing harm to the complainant.

In light of the aforesaid allegations, the complainant seeks relief under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the registration of an FIR (First Information Report) and subsequent investigation into the alleged incident. Additionally, the complainant may also invoke the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for the admissibility and evidentiary value of the complainant's statement and any other relevant evidence.

case_description: A college professor asked a female student for sexual favours in exchange for better grades.
offense_category: sexual harassment and abuse of authority
rephrased_query:
Petition for Inquiry into Allegations of Sexual Harassment and Extortion under the aegis of Article 15 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS): 

Whether the conduct of the college professor, involving a request for sexual favours from a female student in consideration for academic benefits, constitutes an infringement of the student's rights under Article 15(1) BNS, specifically the right to equality and non-discrimination, and whether such conduct falls within the purview of any provision of BNS that prescribes punishment for harassment, intimidation, or exploitation?

 Furthermore, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), 

1. Is a cognizable offence under BNS likely to have been committed, warranting immediate police action, as per Article 20 of BNSS?
2. Should a Magistrate, empowered under Article 40 of BNSS, direct a police investigation into this incident upon receipt of a written complaint from the student, or her legal guardian?

Lastly, considering the relevant provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in relation to the admissibility and evaluation of evidence in such cases, 

3. What constitutes a relevant and admissible piece of evidence, as defined under Article 25 of BSA, to prove the allegations of sexual harassment and extortion against the college professor?

case_description: A man has been following a woman from her office to her home daily, sending unwanted gifts, and watching her through binoculars.
rephrased_query:
**Petition for Relief under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To the Honorable Magistrate,

I, [Name], submit this petition under Article 294(A) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, alleging the commission of an offense by [Offender's Name]. 

It is alleged that [Offender's Name] has been engaging in stalking and harassment of the complainant, causing a reasonable apprehension of harm and distress. This is evident from his daily observation of the complainant from outside her office premises, as well as her residence, through means including but not limited to, the use of binoculars. Furthermore, the complainant has received unwanted gifts from the said offender, which constitutes an unwelcome and uninvited behavior.

I request that this Honorable Court take cognizance of this offense under Article 294(A) and initiate proceedings against [Offender's Name] to prevent further harassment and ensure the safety and well-being of the complainant.

**Verification under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA)**

The complainant is willing to provide evidence and testimony to support the allegations made in this petition. Relevant documents and physical evidence, including photographs, witness statements, and any other relevant materials, are attached herewith.

**Prayer under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)**

I humbly pray to this Honorable Court to grant a restraining order against [Offender's Name] under Article 123(A) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, directing him to cease and desist from any further harassment, stalking, or unwelcome behavior towards the complainant.

**Respectfully submitted**

[Your Name]

case_description: A man grabbed a woman's dupatta and tried to disrobe her in a market while others watched.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 320(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), is the act of the man in grabbing the woman's dupatta and attempting to disrobe her in a public place, where others were present, a case of 'Assault or Use of Criminal Force to Woman with Intent to Outrage her Modesty' as per the definitions stated under Article 12(1) and 12(2) of BNS?

Furthermore, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what would be the appropriate procedure for the registration of an FIR in this incident, and what would be the timeframe for the police to complete the investigation as per Article 159(1) of BNSS, considering the gravity of the offense under BNS?

Additionally, under the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what would be the admissibility of the testimony of the eyewitnesses who witnessed the incident, and how would the court evaluate their credibility in the context of Article 45(1) of BSA?

case_description: A married man had sexual intercourse with his wife during judicial separation against her will.
rephrased_query:
Is the married man liable under the provisions of Article 320(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for the alleged non-consensual sexual intercourse with his wife, who is judicially separated from him, and if so, what are the resultant consequences in accordance with Article 320(2) of the BNS?

Additionally, please provide information on the procedures to be followed under Article 120 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for registering a complaint and obtaining a protection order for the victim in this case, as well as the admissibility and relevance of evidence under Article 60 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in proving the non-consensual nature of the act.

case_description: A man secretly installed a hidden camera in the women's changing room of a gym to record videos.
rephrased_query:
Query for Legal Opinion:

Pursuant to Article 226 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is proposed to enquire into the commission of an offence under Section 228 of BNS, whereby a person, namely [name of accused], allegedly covertly installed a surveillance device, to wit, a hidden camera, within the confines of the women's changing room of a gym, with the intention of capturing video recordings of individuals engaged in a private activity.

It is requested that the following issues be examined under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA):

1. Whether the video recordings captured by the hidden camera constitute admissible evidence under Section 6 of BSA, notwithstanding the clandestine manner in which they were obtained.
